_about: The hosted MCP door's read tools as it serves them, for @onlyworlds/sdk/mcp. Written by scripts/vendor-mcp-tools.mjs from the live door; never edit by hand.
source: https://www.onlyworlds.com/mcp: tools/list, resources/list, resources/templates/list, list_element_types and get_element_schema for each type, asked with the public demo key 0000000001

tools.name: list_element_types
tools.description:
List all 22 OnlyWorlds element types with a one-line shape summary of each.

Every world is built from these types; each element has a stable UUID `id`, a
`name`, and a `type`. Use `get_element_schema(type)` for a type's full field
list. Unauthenticated — schema is public reference. Returns a mapping of the 22
type slugs (the value you pass as `type` to the data tools) to a summary
string.
tools.here: Here it answers on this computer, from the schema as onlyworlds.com served it when this package was built.

tools.name: get_element_schema
tools.description:
Return the field structure of one OnlyWorlds element `type` (a slug from
`list_element_types`, e.g. "character").

The result groups the type's writable fields by kind so a caller knows how to
read and write them: `text` (strings), `integer`, `single_link` (one UUID),
`multi_link` (an array of UUIDs), and `generic` (a type+id pair pointing at any
element type). For every link field the target element type is given under
`link_targets`. All link values are element UUIDs. Unauthenticated. Errors if
`type` is not one of the 22 types.
tools.here: Here it answers on this computer, from the schema as onlyworlds.com served it when this package was built.

tools.name: search_schema
tools.description:
Search every element type's fields for `query` (case-insensitive substring),
across all 22 types. Useful for "which types have a `location` field?" or
finding where a concept lives in the schema.

Returns a mapping of type slug -> the matching field names in that type (types
with no match are omitted); a `query` that also matches a type slug lists that
type with an empty field list so the type-name hit is not lost. Unauthenticated.

tools.name: list_worlds
tools.description:
The worlds you can read here. With an API-Key: the key's one world. Signed
in through a hosted client (a bearer), where this server offers one: every
world your account owns or is a member of, as your account's world list shows
them; pass one's `id` as `world` to the other read tools; a
bearer reads only, and writes need an API-Key and API-Pin. Returns `{data: [{id, slug, name, role}, ...]}`,
`role` being `owner` or your membership's role (co_builder, contributor, guest),
and `slug` the world's public page address, or null.
tools.here: Here it answers from a world folder on this computer, not from onlyworlds.com; `world` is the id in the folder's world.json.

tools.name: get_me
tools.description:
Who you are in this world, and its front door: the same body as
`GET /api/v2/me` for your credential, built by the same function.

Returns GET /me's body: `world` ({id, name}), `scope` (`read` or `write`),
`kind`, `role`, `membership`, `character`, `lenses`, `lenses_from`,
`front_door` and `reading_aids` always; `name` for an AI or a player seat;
`x_served_trimmed` when a lens you chose is left out of `lenses`. `kind` is
`owner`, `person`, `player` (a player seat: a friend reading as one
Character) or `agent` (an AI seat: an AI's own membership and key, which a
person answers for).
Only an AI seat's writes are ever held for review, and only in a world whose
owner chose to review them: there an update, a link edit or a bulk replace is proposed,
not applied (the answer names the `proposal`), for a keeper (the owner or a
co-builder) to accept or decline; a create lands at once, marked
`x_review_proposed`, and lists and searches leave it out unless `include_proposed` is true. Every
other key's writes apply at once.
`front_door.charter` is the id of the world's Charter, the house rules: read
it first, with `get_element("law", id)`.
`front_door.charter_skill` lists the ids of the Objects it names, each
read with `get_element("object", id)`. Each is null, or the list empty,
when there is none you may read. `front_door` also names who answers for
you (`sponsor`, `sponsor_character`), your own Character (`my_character`)
and the seats you answer for (`my_seats`). `reading_aids` is what to read
first, as you read the world: the Charter with its rules and skill, the
Guide, the Domains and the strand. Its Guide, each Domain and each strand
slot is a typed pointer, `{id, type, name}` (a Domain's `hubs` and
front_door's `charter_element` and `charter_skill_elements` are `{type,
id}`): fetch any of them with `get_element(type, id)`. The strand's slots
are `narrative`, `event`, `location`, `character` and `now`, each null when
there is none, beside `same`. Signed in through a hosted client (a
bearer), where this server offers one, it answers as your own read key in
that world answers with no PIN sent; a PIN sent beside the bearer is never
read. Otherwise it requires an
API-Key, and asks of it what GET /api/v2/me asks of it. A PIN sent with a
key is treated exactly as that route treats it: refused where the route
refuses it, counted toward the lockout where the route counts it, ignored
where the route ignores it.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world by its id): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

tools.here: Here it answers from a world folder on this computer, not from onlyworlds.com: as the folder's owner with no account behind it (no membership, Character, sponsor, seats or lenses), with scope read, since these tools never write the folder; `world` is the id in the folder's world.json.

tools.name: list_elements
tools.description:
List elements of one `type` in the world named by your API-Key header,
newest-created first.

`type` is a slug from `list_element_types` (e.g. "character"). Optional
`name_contains` filters by case-insensitive name substring; `supertype` is
trimmed and matched without regard to case, the whole word, as the profiles
read it and as GET /api/v2/{type}?supertype= does (" message " and "MESSAGE"
match Message, "Messages" does not; an empty string lists the elements with
none); `subtype` is read the same way, as ?subtype= does. `ids` (a list of
1 to 200 element ids) keeps only those, as ?ids= does. `created_by` (a
membership id, as GET /api/v2/members lists them, or "owner" for the
owner's own writes) keeps what that member created, as ?created_by= does.
`link` filters by the type's single-link fields, as ?<field>=<id> does: one
object, each key a single-link field of this type (get_element_schema lists
them under `single_link`), each value an element id, or "" for the
elements you are served with none. A key with no member behind it (an
`ow_r_` or `ow_w_` key the owner made, a classic or demo key) or the
owner's own sign-in, a co-builder's, and a contributor's while no element
of the world is hidden are served each stored link, whatever it names, and
match on it. Any other is served a link null where it names no element it
can see, and on an element it knows of only as a stub (`known_of`),
whatever the stub stores; it matches only what it is served: an element it
cannot see gives the same empty list as an id that names nothing.
`list_elements("pin", link={"map": "<map id>"})` lists the pins on one map;
`link={"location": "<id>"}` on a character, the characters there.
`limit` (default 100, max 1000) and `offset` page the result.
Requires a READ or WRITE API-Key. Returns `{data: [element, ...], limit,
offset, has_more, proposed_left_out}` where each element is the full v2 wire
shape and `id` is a UUID. Use `get_element(type, id)` for a single element.
A parlor's room elements (marked `x_room_of`) are left out unless
`include_room` is true, and so are the world's reading aids (its Charter,
Guide and Domains, marked `x_charter_of`). With `include_room` true both come
back. The Charter (the house rules) and the skills it names are in `get_me`'s
`front_door`; a list is never where they are taken from. The strand, the
story this world is about, is the World's `x_strand` mark, not an element: no
list serves it; `get_me`'s `reading_aids` names its elements, each fetched with
`get_element`.
An element carrying x_review_proposed is proposed, not yet reviewed by a
keeper; it is left out unless asked for. Any value counts but null, blank
text, [] and {}. `include_proposed` true serves it whole, mark on: treat it
as proposed, not yet reviewed, never as a fact. A stub (`known_of`) of a
proposed element shows no mark: its being served under `include_proposed`
is the sign.
`proposed_left_out` says how many matching elements were left out (0 with
`include_proposed`).

tools.name: get_element
tools.description:
Fetch one element by `type` and `id` (a UUID) from the world named by your
API-Key header.

`type` is a slug from `list_element_types`. Returns the full v2 wire shape
(the same body as `GET /api/v2/{type}/{id}`): `type`, `id`, `name`, scalar
fields, link fields as UUID arrays, and any extension fields inline. Requires a
READ or WRITE API-Key. Errors if no element of that type with that id exists in
the world.

world.description: The world to read, by id or by its public page's slug. With an API-Key, leave it out (or name the key's own world by its id): a key reads its own world only. list_worlds names the worlds you can read here.

tools.here: Here it answers from a world folder on this computer, not from onlyworlds.com; `world` is the id in the folder's world.json.

tools.name: search_elements
tools.description:
Search the world named by your API-Key header for elements whose name or
text fields (description and each type's prose fields, such as a
Character's background) hold every word of `query` as a whole word,
ignoring case: "ore" does not find "more", and "copper mine" needs both
words somewhere in the element. No stemming.

`query` is 2 to 200 characters. Optional `type` (a slug from
`list_element_types`) searches one type only; `limit` (default 50, clamped
to 1-200) caps the results. Name matches come first, then the rest, each by
type and then by name. Returns `{query, results: [{type, id, name,
supertype, subtype, field, snippet}, ...], count, truncated}`: `field` is
where the words were found (`name` or a text field), `snippet` up to 160
characters of it around the first match, and `truncated` true when more
matched than `limit` (no further pages: narrow the query). `id` is a UUID;
call `get_element(type, id)` for the full body. Requires a READ or WRITE
API-Key; a guest key searches only what it may read. This mirrors
`GET /api/v2/search`, except that a parlor's room elements (marked
`x_room_of`) and the world's reading aids (its Charter, Guide and Domains,
marked `x_charter_of`) are left out unless `include_room` is true, and proposed
elements are too. The Charter (the house rules) and the skills it names are in
`get_me`'s `front_door`; a search is never where they are taken from.
An element carrying x_review_proposed is proposed, not
yet reviewed by a keeper; it is left out unless asked for. Any value but
null counts, an object or not. `include_proposed` true keeps it, its row
carrying `x_review_proposed`: treat it as proposed, not yet reviewed, never
as a fact. A stub's row (`known_of`) of a proposed element shows no mark:
its being served under `include_proposed` is the sign.
`proposed_left_out` says how many matching elements were left out (0 with
`include_proposed`).

resources.name: element_types
resources.description: The 22 OnlyWorlds element types, each with a one-line shape summary (the list_element_types tool's output).

resources.name: world_index
resources.description: The world named by your API-Key header and its elements by type, names and ids only (at most 100 per type by name, `has_more` beyond; a type's full list is the list_elements tool's, in its own order), for picking one to read as onlyworlds://element/{type}/{id}. Proposed elements (x_review_proposed, not yet reviewed by a keeper) are left out and counted in `proposed_left_out`. The Charter and the skills it names are in the get_me tool's `front_door`, never taken from this index.
